sections.h2: How is Alabama organized when you sell a house?
sections.html:
Alabama has 67 counties, and a home sale touches a county office at almost every step. The city on your mailing address matters less than the county the parcel sits in. Wikipedia's municipality list shows Birmingham and Hoover reaching into both Jefferson and Shelby counties.

Most taxable real property is assessed locally by the county assessing official at the courthouse, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue. Two county contacts come up again and again:

  • The revenue commissioner, tax assessor or tax collector, who sets the value, sends the bill and takes payment.
  • The probate office, where deeds are recorded and where estates are opened.

Our pages below are grouped by county. If yours is not listed, the statewide rules still apply and the courthouse can answer local questions. Our Alabama guides by city and county page gathers the same material in one place.

sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill, and when is it late?
sections.html:
The county does, once a year. The Alabama Department of Revenue says the lien date is October 1 and the tax is due the following October 1. Lauderdale County's revenue commissioner describes the same cycle in plainer terms: due October 1, delinquent after December 31, advertised for sale in April and sold at a tax sale in May.

How much you owe starts with the class your house falls into. Lauderdale County lists three classes, and your bill is built from the assessed value after any exemption.

ClassWhat it coversAssessment percentage
Class IUtility property30 percent
Class IIAll other property, such as a rental house20 percent
Class IIIAgricultural, timber and single-family owner-occupied10 percent

Millage rates are set locally, so call your county revenue office for the exact rate.

If the tax goes unpaid, the house can be sold at auction. Mobile County's revenue commission says the owner then has three years to redeem, with interest of 12 percent a year compounded daily, and after that the owner has to deal with the buyer directly. Selling before the auction keeps more options open. See our Alabama tax sale guide and Alabama property tax guide for appeals and for selling with tax due.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption affect a sale?
sections.html:
It lowers the tax bill while you live in the house, and it can also change foreclosure rules. The Department of Revenue defines a homestead as a single-family, owner-occupied dwelling and its land, up to 160 acres, that is your primary residence on the first day of the tax year.

  • Under 65 and not disabled: up to $4,000 of assessed value at the state level, and up to $2,000 at the county level.
  • Age 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or blind: different limits apply, and some depend on income.
  • To apply, visit your local county office. The department's page gives no filing deadline, so ask the county.

Whether you have claimed a homestead exemption matters later in this guide, because it can shorten the redemption period after a foreclosure. Details are on our Alabama homestead exemption page.

sections.h2: Is foreclosure judicial in Alabama, and how long do you have to act?
sections.html:
Lenders can go either way, but most residential foreclosures are non-judicial, meaning no lawsuit and no judge before the auction. Nolo's Alabama summary says the lender publishes notice in a newspaper once a week for three consecutive weeks before the sale. Alabama Code section 35-10-13 requires that notice to run in a newspaper published in the county where the land sits, and to state when and where the sale will happen, its terms and a description of the property.

After the auction, the law gives some people a chance to take the house back:

  • Debtors, mortgagors, their spouses and their children or heirs may redeem under section 6-5-248.
  • For residential property where a homestead exemption was claimed for the sale year, redemption must happen within 180 days, and the clock starts only after the lender gives the required notice.
  • For other property the deadline is one year after the sale, and redemption can never run past one year.

Nolo adds that staying past ten days after a written demand for possession can cost the right to redeem, and that a lender can sue for any shortfall. If a notice of sale has been published, talk to a foreclosure attorney or a HUD-approved housing counselor soon.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed, and who handles the closing?
sections.html:
Two charges apply. The Department of Revenue lists a recordation tax of $0.50 per $500 of value, or fraction thereof, on deeds, and $0.15 per $100 of indebtedness on mortgages. The probate office then charges its own recording fee. Lauderdale County's probate office lists $16 for the first page and $3 for each added page, with $1 for each grantor or grantee past two. That schedule carries a 2012 date, so confirm current amounts with your county.

ItemAmount shown by the source
Deed tax$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction thereof
Mortgage tax$0.15 per $100 of indebtedness
Recording, first page (Lauderdale County)$16
Recording, each added page (Lauderdale County)$3

On a $200,000 house that rate gives $200 of deed tax. Who pays is a matter for the contract. Stewart Title's Alabama practice page says the owner's policy, transfer tax, recording fee, survey and closing fees fall to whatever the buyer and seller negotiate.

The same page says searching title, closing and disbursing do not have to be handled by an attorney, yet any legal document, a deed included, must be drafted by an Alabama attorney unless a party is drafting it for themselves. Lauderdale County also requires the preparer's name and address on the instrument.

sections.h2: How does an inherited house move through probate?
sections.html:
Through the probate court in the county where the person lived. Mobile County's probate court describes the usual path: a petition is filed, the court grants Letters of Administration, a claims notice is published weekly for three weeks, and creditors generally file claims within six months. The estate cannot be divided until claims and expenses are paid, which takes at least six months.

For a seller, the key point is authority. The same page lists selling real estate among the actions a personal representative cannot take without prior court authorization.

  • Ask the county probate office which forms it requires, and whether the house can be sold during administration.
  • Gather the death certificate and the will if there is one.
  • Pull the latest property tax bill, since taxes keep accruing while the estate is open.

Our pages on Alabama probate and selling inherited property and Alabama estate and inheritance tax go into more detail.

sections.h2: What if the house has a tenant in it?
sections.html:
A sale does not remove the tenant, so a lease and any eviction case have to be sorted out first. Evictions in Alabama are unlawful detainer actions. The Montgomery County court's guide says district court and circuit court share jurisdiction, and that the tenant is owed written notice with a right to cure: seven business days for unpaid rent and fourteen days for other lease violations. A landlord who files pays a $350 initial filing fee, and the tenant has seven days to answer a possession complaint.

If the tenant appeals, the deadline is seven consecutive days, and staying in the house during the appeal requires posting a bond with the circuit court clerk. Read our eviction process guide and landlord and tenant rules before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What does an as-is cash sale mean in Alabama?
sections.html:
It means you sell the house in its present condition and do not pay for repairs first. Alabama is a caveat emptor state, so Nolo reports that sellers generally have no duty to volunteer problems. There are limits. A seller must disclose a material defect that the buyer cannot readily see and the seller knows about, must answer buyer questions honestly, and must follow federal lead paint disclosure rules. Alabama does not require a seller disclosure form, though agents often attach one anyway.

A plain written list of known issues is the safest route.

sections.h2: Which property problems come up in Alabama?
sections.html:
Two are worth checking before you list or sell.

  • Radon. The Alabama Department of Public Health says high radon has been found in every state, Alabama included, and recommends fixing homes at or above 4 pCi/L. It names 15 counties with the highest potential: Calhoun, Clay, Cleburne, Colbert, Coosa, Franklin, Jackson, Jefferson, Lauderdale, Lawrence, Limestone, Madison, Morgan, Shelby and Talladega.
  • Flooding. A FEMA statement reported by Insurance Journal calls flooding Alabama's second most common natural hazard. The same article says only about 57,000 of an estimated 1.8 million Alabama households had flood insurance.

Neither one stops a sale. Ask the county about flood zone maps for your parcel.

faqs.q: How many counties does Alabama have?
faqs.a: Alabama has 67 counties. Property tax, deed recording and probate all run through county offices, so start with the county where the house sits.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due each October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. Unpaid accounts can be advertised in April and sold at a tax sale in May, according to Lauderdale County.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a house after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Mobile County's revenue commission says three years from the sale, with interest of 12 percent a year. Other counties may post their own procedures, so call yours.
Lenders may use either route, but most residential foreclosures are non-judicial. Notice runs in a local newspaper once a week for three weeks before the sale.

faqs.q: How much is the Alabama deed tax?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue lists $0.50 per $500 of value or fraction thereof. The probate office adds its own recording fee.

faqs.q: Does an attorney have to close a house sale in Alabama?
faqs.a: A closing does not have to be handled by an attorney, but deeds and other legal documents must be drafted by an Alabama attorney unless a party drafts them for themselves.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Often not without court authority. A personal representative needs prior court authorization to sell real estate, so ask the probate office first.
